# Batch API

`POST /api/batch`

Runs several record writes in one database transaction: if any fails, none of them is kept. Each one is checked like
the same request on its own (the collection's rules, your hooks).

Batch requests are off until you turn them on: **Settings → Application → Batch API**, or `PATCH /api/settings` with
`{"batch": {"enabled": true, "maxRequests": 50, "timeout": 3}}`.

| Body | |
|---|---|
| `requests` | the writes, in order: each a `method`, a `url` (a Records API path), and its `body` (and optional `headers`) |

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/batch \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "requests": [
      {"method": "POST", "url": "/api/collections/orders/records", "body": {"total": 42}},
      {"method": "PATCH", "url": "/api/collections/products/records/p4x8m2k1z9q0w3e", "body": {"stock-": 1}},
      {"method": "DELETE", "url": "/api/collections/carts/records/c7n2b5v8x1z4q6r"}
    ]
  }'
```

It answers one result per request, in order:

```json
[
  { "status": 200, "body": { "collectionName": "orders", "id": "o1a2b3c4d5e6f7g", "total": 42 } },
  { "status": 200, "body": { "collectionName": "products", "id": "p4x8m2k1z9q0w3e", "stock": 9 } },
  { "status": 204, "body": null }
]
```

If one fails, the whole batch answers `400`, with the failed request's index and error in `data`.

The urls may only be the Records API's create, update, upsert (`PUT /api/collections/{collection}/records`, which
creates or updates by the body's `id`) and delete. To upload files in a batch, send `multipart/form-data` with the
JSON in a `@jsonPayload` field and each file as `requests.N.fieldName`.
